decisions.title: Keep payment processor access optional and isolated
decisions.proposal: Keep card access optional and isolated from Bitcoin authority through a replaceable adapter. Do not require processor enrollment for cash or direct Bitcoin receiving.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Complete a retail checkout using the tender the merchant has enabled, with a correct sale ledger and receipt.
decisions.rationale: The standalone product includes optional third-party card processing. Its account, credential and payment lifecycle must remain separate from merchant Bitcoin keys and authority.
decisions.user_authorization_status: Established direction: optional card processing, cash, merchant Bitcoin authority and independent recovery. The adapter set, eligibility, hardware and exact setup experience remain undecided.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Review provider credential scopes and data flows; test unknown/canceled/refund outcomes; demonstrate that revoking card access leaves cash and direct Bitcoin receiving available.

decisions.title: Do not require company server permission for local checkout or recovery
decisions.proposal: Keep a usable standalone local sale and on-chain receive path without company login/approval, publisher ledger or telemetry. Any server-backed integration stays opt-in and scoped; it cannot become a hidden prerequisite for recovery.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Operate a register, receive Bitcoin, and recover keys and sale records after routine service/device failure.
decisions.rationale: Accepted purity position rejects mandatory company-server approval for recovery, telemetry, or sales-history upload; however remote-sync UX and support model remain design questions.
decisions.user_authorization_status: established constraint: no required company permission over Bitcoin funds and independent recovery. A company endpoint is not required for standalone/local cash and on-chain operation per current plan; optional service UX remains undecided.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Demonstrate standalone cash/on-chain checkout and recovery with company endpoints unavailable; review each opt-in sync, webhook or backup service before adding.

decisions.title: Evaluate bounded owner-approved signing and UTXO protection
decisions.proposal: Preserve the current signing behavior in code while researching owner-approved bounded signing/automation for UTXO protection, fee budgets, reservations, and routine approved transactions. Define explicit transaction/value/fee/destination bounds, owner control, safe failure and recovery before implementing any change.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Protect merchant funds from uneconomic UTXOs or operational mistakes while allowing an owner to authorize routine transfers and refunds safely.
decisions.rationale: The current code exposes advisory-only UTXO guidance, but that is an implementation boundary, not a permanent rejection of protection or automation. The user said an earlier signing-control proposal was acceptable; architecture evidence and review remain necessary.
decisions.user_authorization_status: research candidate: bounded owner-approved signing control was acceptable in principle. No exact policy, automatic coin selection, consolidation, fee limits, or signing behavior change has been approved for implementation.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Produce and review a threat model, limits, authority map, state machine, failure recovery, fee/UTXO evidence and transaction-display proof; obtain approval for exact behavior before changing signing.

decisions.title: Separate recurring payment requests from standing wallet debit authority
decisions.proposal: Preserve subscription plans, cycle invoices, lifecycle notices and merchant-authorized refunds. Default recurring Bitcoin billing to a fresh customer-initiated request per cycle; do not claim a universal wallet can be auto-debited. Research any opt-in recurring spending authority separately with explicit limits, consent, revocation, destination scope and failure handling.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Bill a customer on a recurring schedule, let them pay each due cycle, manage subscription changes, and resolve missed payments or refunds.
decisions.rationale: Invoice/subscription workflows exist, but URI or invoice creation does not authorize a merchant to spend from a customer self-custody wallet. Preserving the billing job does not require assuming pull-payment capability.
decisions.user_authorization_status: merchant recurring billing job is in scope for research; customer-authorized invoice flow is a candidate. Universal automatic debit is not an established user constraint or approved mechanism.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Validate repeat invoice lifecycle and customer initiation first. Any reusable debit authority requires explicit user approval, protocol/wallet compatibility, clear consent/revocation, bounded amount/frequency, and recovery/dispute policy.

decisions.title: Treat fee and UTXO automation as a bounded protection candidate
decisions.proposal: Current UTXO fee guidance is advisory only. Research protection that can block, reserve, or request approval around uneconomic outputs and fee budgets, including bounded owner-approved transaction automation; do not infer autonomous spend authority or promise zero fees/guaranteed confirmation.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Explain what a receipt is worth now and what it may cost to spend later.
decisions.rationale: The plan describes the current code boundary as advisory with no autonomous selection/consolidation. That does not veto future automation. User accepted a signing-control proposal in principle; implementation requires exact bounds and architecture proof.
decisions.user_authorization_status: research candidate: UTXO protection and bounded owner-approved automation are acceptable for architecture study; current code remains advisory-only. Exact policy and implementation approval remain open.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Specify value and fee thresholds, privacy effects, reversibility, exception path, recovery, actual fee variance and owner controls; reviewed design before implementation.

decisions.title: Keep Shop Lightning as a core Bitcoin goal with an honest readiness path
decisions.proposal: Treat Shop Lightning as a core receiving goal, opt-in in merchant setup, with capital, inbound-liquidity, availability, persistence/recovery and independent-exit gates. On-chain-first release ordering is a proposed sequencing option; it does not defer the long-term Shop Lightning product goal. Avoid free/prepaid-liquidity and guaranteed-route claims.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Receive Bitcoin over a fast channel at the merchant’s own receiving node, and retain a safe on-chain recovery path.
decisions.rationale: The user’s product goal includes Shop Lightning; the standalone plan requires capacity/funding/availability/recovery gates. Those gates preserve honest economics without turning a proposed first-release order into product exclusion.
decisions.user_authorization_status: established goal: Shop Lightning receiving. Setup, liquidity source, exact release sequence and device coverage remain proposals to prove; no specific provider or free-liquidity assumption is approved.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Demonstrate node setup, actual funding and inbound capacity, recurring operation, backups, restore, peer/provider loss, route failures, channel exit, timelock and on-chain fees on the chosen version/device.

decisions.title: Do not promise offline Bitcoin settlement
decisions.proposal: When offline, continue only locally supported sale recording and cash tender. Show an on-chain request as awaiting observation and Lightning as unavailable when node status is stale. Keep card offline behavior provider-specific and report pending/unknown until reconciled.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Continue a cashier interaction during connectivity loss without claiming money arrived or fulfilling twice.
decisions.rationale: Bitcoin settlement requires network/node observation or later reconciliation; cached invoice/QR is not payment proof. Existing plan requires honest Bitcoin observation states and treats missing responses as unknown.
decisions.user_authorization_status: established requirement: do not misstate Bitcoin settlement when disconnected or stale. Cash fallback and tender-specific offline UX are supported job candidates; exact device behavior remains to validate.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Network/node interruption, device restart, duplicate attempts and reconnect reconciliation on target hardware; verify no false paid state or duplicate fulfillment.

decisions.title: Keep privacy local-first and multi-location optional
decisions.proposal: Keep customer identity and sales history local by default, use minimal payment-request metadata, and make multi-location synchronization or webhooks explicit opt-in with location-scoped permissions and disclosed data fields.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Complete private local checkout and reconcile each merchant location; offer an optional shared view when the owner chooses it.
decisions.rationale: Accepted purity position rules out required telemetry and sales-history upload, while the standalone plan defers universal multi-location claims. Optional service design remains undecided.
decisions.user_authorization_status: Established privacy direction: no mandatory publisher telemetry or sales-history upload. Multi-location release support has not been established; optional synchronization and customer-profile design remain proposals.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Threat/data-flow review, export and webhook preview, location access matrix, retention choice, and offline behavior before enabling any shared service.

decisions.title: Treat card acceptance as replaceable and production-gated
decisions.proposal: Use the existing Square Sandbox flow as the adapter starting point, retain a provider-neutral tender interface, and do not claim production card acceptance until account, country, device, reader, outage, refund, reconciliation and privacy gates pass.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Accept cards when the merchant’s chosen provider and physical workflow are supported; preserve cash and Bitcoin choices if card service fails.
decisions.rationale: Accepted plan explicitly bounds current evidence to virtual-card Sandbox and avoids provider/country/device eligibility claims without fresh evidence.
decisions.user_authorization_status: established_constraint: card optional; production readiness unproven pending gates. A final vendor or adapter selection remains undecided.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Fresh provider eligibility evidence and an end-to-end physical reader shift including lost responses, duplicate submissions, refunds, revocation, force-stop and relaunch.

decisions.title: Use standalone retail as the first measured validation scope
decisions.proposal: Prioritize a complete standalone retail shift and validate sale, tenders, exception handling, receipts, refunds, staff authority and closeout. Treat restaurant, online, unattended and multi-location capabilities as backlog and evidence targets, not rejected jobs or a permanent product boundary. POS integrations follow as proposed sequencing.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Serve merchants who sell at a counter today and preserve their path to restaurant, online or multi-location workflows as their needs and validation evidence justify.
decisions.rationale: The plan positions standalone retail before integrations and requires measured evidence; it does not establish a final ceiling on product scope. Existing POS later is the accepted sequence, while target workflows beyond retail remain future research.
decisions.user_authorization_status: Established sequence: standalone product before existing-POS integrations. A retail shift is the proposed first validation scenario; the exact release scope and later adapter priority remain undecided.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Complete a target retail shift, then gather merchant evidence for restaurant/online/multi-location jobs and evaluate the next workflow and integration independently.

decisions.title: Use familiar operational controls without cloning every incumbent feature
decisions.proposal: Use incumbent research to identify familiar merchant jobs and recovery cues—refunds, staff controls, split tender, local outage recovery, receipts, and closeout—then design Bitcoin-specific states and permissions around self-custody. Do not reject merchant jobs merely because one incumbent uses a custodial, hosted, or fiat mechanism.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Cashiers can finish, void, refund, hand off and close a shift with understandable status and manageable exception steps.
decisions.rationale: A vendor’s mechanism is not the merchant job. Better UX remains an empirical design question and must preserve established authority/purity goals.
decisions.user_authorization_status: research gate: merchant UX jobs are candidates for observation; exact screens/defaults are undecided. Self-custody and independent recovery remain established constraints.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Cashier observation and usability tasks with named retail workflow; measure completion time, error rate, exception recovery, receipt accuracy and training burden before design commitment.

decisions.title: Reject mandatory custodial Square Bitcoin and forced fiat conversion by default
decisions.proposal: Treat a Square-style custodial Bitcoin purchase/acceptance flow, fiat conversion, altcoin settlement or required processor account as a mechanism exception requiring separate consent. Default architecture remains direct Bitcoin receipt to merchant keys. Preserve merchant jobs of direct receive, Bitcoin refund to an owner-approved fresh destination, recurring subscription invoices and related lifecycle management; do not silently replace those jobs with gift-card/fiat/processor credit.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Take Bitcoin directly, retain authority and independent recovery, refund Bitcoin under merchant-approved rules, and bill subscriptions on a clear recurring schedule.
decisions.rationale: A hosted mechanism may simplify quote, conversion or reporting, but changes custody, funds permission and settlement asset. User-established boundaries favor self-custody, no required company funds permission, and Bitcoin-first product intent.
decisions.user_authorization_status: established constraint: self-custody, independent recovery, Bitcoin-first and no required company funds permission. Custodial Square Bitcoin, forced fiat conversion and altcoin substitution are not authorized as defaults; no product job is rejected.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Only consider a specific custodial/conversion exception after explicit authorization, complete terms and authority map, asset and fees disclosure, refund/subscription path, exit plan, and direct self-custody fallback.
